jobs.title: Lot C, v
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 21, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; THE GUARD — middle-aged man in a dark campus security windbreaker and cap, clipboard, standing bent slightly as if to a car window. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Monday. A space opens in Lot B. The guard holds it. Wood drives past it into C. The guard nods, and tears the ticket he'd already written. Panel 1: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a security guard standing in an open parking space near a building waving a rusted small car toward it (in this panel: THE GUARD). Guard says "Here! B! I held it!". Panel 2: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a rusted small car driving slowly past a waving guard, the young driver's face apologetic and certain, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a car parked alone in a far lot while a small distant guard tears a page off his clipboard, no words (in this panel: THE GUARD, WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a guard at a car window speaking to a young man, a torn ticket in his hand (in this panel: THE GUARD, WOOD). Guard says "Wrote you up Thursday. Loitering.". Wood says "And?". Guard says "Tore it. You're not loitering. You're — what was it.". Wood says "Auditing.". Guard says "Right.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17.
